challenge.archive-handoff.md:
# Mixed selection archive proposal

In the seed `archive-one` in `cases.jsonl`, archiving the selection and clearing every active note both produce `[]`. Archiving only the first selected note also gives that answer. The singleton cannot distinguish these behaviors.

For Bootstrap review, consider one hand-authored variant of the seed, `archive-mixed-two` revision 1. Start with active notes `[A, B, C, D]`, select `[B, D]`, and request archive once. All four notes start active. Two survivors make display order observable.

| Hypothetical remaining notes | Proposed interpretation under owner.md |
| --- | --- |
| `[A, C]` or `[C, A]` | Accept either. Both selected notes are gone and each unselected note remains active once. |
| `[]` | Reject. Clearing all notes also removed A and C. |
| `[A, C, D]` | Reject. Archiving only B left D active. |
| `[A, D]` | Reject. The survivor count is right, but C is missing and D is still active. |

Keep the singleton as the clean control. Compare survivor identities and multiplicities from the same starting state for each alternative. The current `grade.py` sorts the submitted and expected lists before comparison, so either valid order fits the existing rule. It scores a supplied list and provides no independent observation of an archive operation.

The reviewer requested fixed display order and a score for repeat archive. The owner calls order a preference, so an order-sensitive check would reject a legitimate result. The owner leaves repeat archive undecided. Defer scoring a second invocation until the owner specifies what happens when an already archived note is targeted again.

This is an unexecuted development proposal in the singleton's construction family. No candidate output, activation, observed score, or confirmed finding exists. The parent can review the proposed expectation against `owner.md` and the approved decision in `release-history.tsv`. The reviewer suggestions concern criteria and supply no human outcome labels.

correct.SCENARIOS.md:
# Archive situations

The owner correction in [owner.md](owner.md) makes the number of selected notes determine what one Archive invocation does. The IDs below also identify the development rows in [cases.jsonl](cases.jsonl). Both belong to the archive-one construction family.

| Situation ID and revision | Starting situation | Owner expectation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| archive-one, revision 1 | A is active and selected. Invoke Archive once. | Archive A. The active list is empty. |
| archive-mixed-two, revision 2 | A, B, C and D are active. Select B and D and invoke Archive once. | Preview the selection. All four notes stay active, each exactly once, in any order. |

Revision 2 replaces revision 1’s expected survivors A and C for the same input. The preview rule applies to selections of two or more notes. Display order remains a preference. The owner has left repeated Archive undecided, so repeat invocations remain outside scoring.

The grader checks only the supplied remaining list. It cannot observe the preview or establish what the product did.

audit.release-audit.md:
# Release scoring review

The owner correction, SCENARIOS.md and ledger decision 4 govern archive-mixed-two revision 2. With A, B, C and D active and B and D selected, one Archive invocation previews the selection. Every original ID must remain exactly once, in any order. The singleton still archives A. Repeat invocation is undecided. Both rows are development cases in the archive-one family. A remaining-list score can address only the reported survivors.

## Replay

Each cell records stdout from a fresh Python process in the project root. Replay any cell with `python3 SCRIPT ROW 'JSON'`, substituting its column heading, row ID and literal submission. The expected column follows the owner correction. All commands exited 0.

| Row | JSON submission | Expected | release_grade.py | grade.py (historical comparator) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| archive-mixed-two | `["A","B","C","D"]` | True | True | True |
| archive-mixed-two | `["D","C","B","A"]` | True | True | True |
| archive-mixed-two | `["A","A","B","C"]` | False | True | False |
| archive-mixed-two | `["A","B","C","X"]` | False | True | False |
| archive-mixed-two | `["A","C"]` | False | False | False |
| archive-mixed-two | `["A","B","C","D","D"]` | False | False | False |
| archive-one | `[]` | True | True | True |
| archive-one | `["A"]` | False | False | False |

## Frozen inputs

Runtime was Python 3.14.9. SHA-256 at replay time follows.

```
49b7843eafdccd0deca93612375427255fda20c5b5d449f7eedabdeeeedc237b  release_grade.py
996ffdb2ec350d299bfc7eb8ad0f55652fe3613ac18bc137dc1c159337c7bb0a  grade.py
57b672057cd842e72c0300502cdcabe17449a9e633229c2d7ecf11904a5fb1ed  cases.jsonl
0cdab8a6f93e7a4f9af0dec76cf5afdb5aa8c856bbf48d18eb8342cfc6b048a2  owner.md
8b8dcb2de1859c020344b49d328bb2fe6cfc86d589f2e27a1d335f711003aaf8  SCENARIOS.md
660007b86e5c64c25d9f60771ffe6ea941053c42917bd8f6e4c69f3619dc3b7f  skills/cross-examine/SKILL.md
db283bf0a3dcb6dd27889d7dc9bb473488e25262966d30fb0c9a122ebc8e0caa  release-history.tsv
```

The ledger digest covers decisions 1 through 4, before the audit entry.

## Finding and next decision

For archive-mixed-two revision 2, replacing D with X changes one ID and preserves the length. Release scoring returned True. It also accepted A twice with D missing. The expression `len(result) == len(row['remaining'])` discards both identity and multiplicity. The obsolete revision 1 answer was rejected because its length is two. Passing that negative control cannot resolve the dispute.

These were operator replays through the ordinary submission argument. Each invocation read the same project fixture. There were no candidate runs, separate attackers, product executions, or preview observations. The operator also assessed the proposed correction. No independent reviewer was available. Intent review is **unreviewed**. The observations establish a discrepancy in supplied-list scoring on a development row. No particular disputed submission was supplied for attribution.

**Pending owner decision.** Hold reliance on this score for survivor correctness. Decide whether to adopt order-insensitive comparison of ID multiplicities for list submissions and retain the duplicate/missing-ID and reverse-order inputs as release checks. On these inputs the existing comparator rejected both substitutions and accepted both valid orders and the singleton baseline. Those are comparative replays. Release integration and a repaired release score remain unverified. A proposed generation lesson is to pair a reordered positive control with an equal-length ID substitution whenever a collection must preserve membership. The grader, cases and skill guidance await explicit adoption approval. A fresh reviewer would still need to assess any frozen repair before independent validation.
